name: MS DHCP Extended Management
description: Manage Microsoft DHCP servers (IPv4 and IPv6): scopes, options, reservations, failover and a full configuration check.
long_description: Connects to a Microsoft DHCP server (IPv4 and DHCPv6) with the current account, stored credentials or a different login and keeps the failover partners in view. Servers used regularly are kept as favourites in a collapsible list with folders next to the login (e.g. one folder per customer), each with its own login – including a password stored encrypted in the vault – and connection settings; double-click connects. Every scope opens in its own tab with general settings, address pool, options, reservations, exclusions, leases and failover state; findings (errors, warnings, best practice) are calculated while you type and mark the affected fields. New scopes are created from a draft or duplicated from an existing scope, with addresses converted to the new network. Changes on failover scopes can be replicated to the partner automatically (works even when the partner is only reachable via RPC, like the DHCP console). Further pages: server options of every failover server with sync state, failover relationships (expandable to both servers) with all scopes of each server, option definitions (expert mode, locked by default) and a server-wide scan with distribution of findings that also compares everything with the failover partners (scopes, pools, exclusions, options, reservations, relationship settings, classes and definitions). Changes made by others (DHCP console, PowerShell, colleagues) are detected: before saving the tool checks whether the scope was changed since loading, an optional auto-refresh reloads the views, and the server's event log shows who changed what – also as its own page with reading aids (area, action, scope, object and a note per event). Every change runs as a transaction: if a step fails or the action is cancelled, everything already changed is undone automatically, on the server and on the partner. DHCPv6 with the same scope: prefixes, lifetimes, options, reservations by DUID and IAID, exclusions, leases, check, transactions and conflict detection; an IPv4/IPv6 switch selects the view. Optionally the check compares reservations and leases with DNS (name, address, PTR). Detects read-only access (DHCP Users) and hides editing functions accordingly. Talks to the server directly via the Windows DHCP API (RPC) – no PowerShell or WinRM. Replication to the partner uses netsh dhcp from the RSAT DHCP tools (added automatically during installation).
author: KuroShiro
